what: Handset photograph of the DarwinBoot hand-off page: the real loader ran from the phone's own EFI files and handed control to the kernel

darwinboot_lines: DARWINBOOT: payload from another volume 0 of 0
DARWINBOOT: ARM64 va=0xFFFFFFF004004000 pa=0x27004000 args=0x2BAE0000 entry=0x2B..
DARWINBOOT: video base=0x400000 display=1 row=4320 width=1080 height=1920 depth=32
DARWINBOOT: inputs validated; exiting boot services
observations.loader_bar: green bar across the top is present in the photograph
observations.kernel_bar: no bottom green bar is visible in this photograph
observations.console_text: no kernel console output is visible on the panel in this photograph

reading: The chain this port builds runs on the handset up to and including the branch to XNU: the loader read its config, selected the xnu entry, printed the DarwinBoot hand-off page, exited boot services and reports handing off.
The video geometry the loader reports is the hardware's own: base 0x400000, 1080x1920, row 4320 bytes, 32 bpp. It matches the earlier control-mark measurement and differs from the emulator's 800x600.

The photograph does not show kernel console output or the post-MMU bottom bar, so it does not establish that the kernel executed -- it establishes that the loader handed off. Whether the screen stayed on this page, changed, or the device reset was not recorded.

SCTLR_EL1 0xC01B0D and TCR_EL1 0x280003518 are the handset's own values at hand-off; the emulator reports different ones (0x30D0198D / 0x280803518), which is why the kernel's early assumptions have to be checked against the handset rather than the emulator.
